title: Write a rejection message on-call can act on

blocks.text: A bank's transfer API rejects transfers outside its per-transfer limits, which differ by customer tier and change a few times a year. When a business customer calls to ask why a payment was refused, support pastes the log line into a ticket and on-call answers from it. The ticket system is read by a hundred people at an outsourcing partner.

Finish `rejection` in `src/main/java/practice/TransferLimits.java`: the message of the exception that rejects a transfer. From the message alone, on-call must be able to tell what was wrong with the transfer and find it again, and the ticket must be safe to share. About two lines.

cases.says: transfers of exactly the minimum and the maximum go through, and one below the minimum is rejected
a rejection's message contains the rejected amount and the transfer's id
the message gives both limits, so the reader knows what would have been accepted
the message holds no API token and no account number, even though the request carries them

origin.section: A Message Names the Bad Value and the Range It Expected, and Nothing Secret

concepts: A rejection message gives the bad value, the accepted range and an identifier, so the log alone tells what was wrong.
Concatenating a whole request into a message copies every component (a record's toString() prints them all) into every log and ticket; secrets and personal data never go in a message.
